Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroForge Dynamics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroForge Dynamics' Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; and Jennifer Hale, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those discussed today.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. AeroForge Dynamics delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across commercial aerospace, defense, and services. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering long-term value to our shareholders. Today, I will cover the following key areas:

1. Commercial aircraft delivery rates and recovery trajectory: We achieved 142 deliveries in Q3, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially, with year-to-date at 412 units on pace for 550 to 580 full-year, reflecting a strong V-shaped recovery amid supply chain progress.

2. Revenue by segment: commercial aerospace, defense, and services (YoY % change): Total revenue hit $26.4 billion, up 11% YoY, with commercial aerospace at 18% growth, defense steady at 6%, and services surging 25%.

3. Backlog growth (absolute and % change): Record $185 billion total backlog, up significantly year-over-year, with funded backlog growing robustly and book-to-bill above 1.2x across segments.

4. Free cash flow generation and utilization: Q3 FCF of $1.2 billion, YTD $2.8 billion up 25%, deployed toward debt reduction, shareholder returns, and growth investments.

5. Aftermarket and services revenue growth (YoY % change): Strong 25% YoY increase to $3.6 billion, driven by higher flight hours and digital services adoption.

6. Performance of priority defense programs: Excellent execution on F-35, hypersonics like PrSM, and space architectures, with revenue up 16% and margins expanding.

7. Discussion of geopolitical factors affecting defense spending: Tailwinds from NATO spending surges, Indo-Pacific tensions, and U.S. budget growth fueling our international backlog.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to position us as a leader in next-generation air dominance for decades to come. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily as air traffic normalizes.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $26.4 billion, representing an 11% increase year-over-year. Our diluted earnings per share were $7.20. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $15 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at $105 to $110 billion in revenue and $28 to $29 in EPS. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives like advanced manufacturing and R&D. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through our quarterly dividend and ongoing share repurchases under our $4 billion authorization.

Our specific financial highlights include a gross margin of 22.5%, operating income of $4.2 billion, and free cash flow of $1.2 billion.

Building on Michael's overview, let me provide more color starting with our commercial aircraft division, the cornerstone of our recovery story in this robust post-pandemic demand environment. In Q3, we achieved deliveries of 142 aircraft across our portfolio—a 28% increase year-over-year from 111 units in Q3 2023 and a 12% sequential uptick from Q2's 127. Year-to-date through Q3, we stand at 412 deliveries, tracking toward full-year guidance of 550 to 580 units, a 35% jump from 2023's 428 total. By platform, our 737 MAX family led with 98 deliveries at an average 32 per month, the 787 Dreamliner added 28, and regional jets plus freighter conversions contributed 16 more. This reflects disciplined ramp-up to 85% of our narrowbody targets.

Pre-COVID in 2019, we ran above 700 annualized deliveries with 737 output over 50 monthly; pandemic lows hit 11 per month in Q2 2020. Today, air traffic shows a V-shaped recovery—IATA reports global RPKs at 96% of 2019 levels in September, narrowbody utilization at 102%. Our cadence accelerated from 25 monthly in Q4 2022 to 47 now, with Q4 projected at 160 deliveries via backlog conversion.

Supply chain constraints persist, especially engine availability—Pratt & Whitney GTF issues on A320neo ripple to our 737 MAX via shared vendors, and GE LEAP-1B lags limit us to 38 versus 52 monthly. We've countered with dual-sourcing, adding 15% CFM capacity via contracts, reaching 92% on-time from suppliers like Spirit AeroSystems and Triumph, up from 72%.

Regionally, Asia-Pacific took 42% of Q3 deliveries, China 35 units with 737 MAX grabbing 60% single-aisle share from Air China and Juneyao; 2025 growth forecast at 25% on $45 billion backlog. Europe stabilized at 28% with Ryanair and easyJet despite Airbus hiccups; North America 22% via Southwest's 50 MAX 8s; Middle East 5% with Emirates 787s; India and Southeast Asia upside from IndiGo's 500+ order amid 30% traffic growth.

We've invested $1.2 billion in Renton and Spirit for digital FAL using Siemens NX, cutting 737 takt time 25% to 14 days from 21. Our Mach 2 program with Palantir AI yields 18% labor gains amid shortages. Sustainability: 40% Q3 deliveries with ecoDemonstrator for 15% fuel savings, ahead of 777X cert.

Commercial backlog $285 billion—8.5 years at current rates, 65% narrowbody, 12% pricing uplift. Aftermarket MRO up 22% to $2.1 billion aids FCF for NGAD R&D. Risks like GTF inspections mitigated by $10 billion inventory. Guide 650-700 deliveries 2025, ramping to 800+ by 2027, margins to 14% from 9%.

Next, our revenue breakdown by segment. Commercial aerospace was 38% of total at $10.1 billion, up 18% YoY on airline modernization and traffic surge. Deliveries of Horizon 737 equivalents and Apex 777X derivatives hit 145, beating guidance by 10. OEM sales up 25%, eased titanium and composites bottlenecks from Spirit and Hexcel.

North America 55% with 22% lift from Delta/United; Asia-Pacific +35% via Air China's 50 Horizons as China hits 95% 2019 RPKs; Europe +12% despite A320neo delays, boosted by SAF components—FAA STCs underway for 100% SAF on LEAP equivalents ahead of 2027 net-zero. $1.2 billion in additive nacelles cuts lead times 30%; backlog $65 billion, book-to-bill 1.4x.

Defense, 48% at $12.7 billion, up 6% YoY lapping tough comps from F-35 Lot 15. FY24 NDAA's $849 billion funds hypersonics like Dark Eagle at Mach 5+ testing, RDT&E up 15% to $2.8 billion. Missiles/JASSM-ER up 10% to $4.2 billion on $61 billion Ukraine aid, 150/month rates.

International +12% to $3.5 billion: Saudi Vision 2030 $1.2 billion PAC-3; Japan/Australia F-35. Offset inflation with $800 million digital twins for 25% MRO gains. Backlog $95 billion, FY25 $29.8 billion hypersonics/space; Starshield at 20% share.

Services, 14% at $3.6 billion, +25% YoY fastest growth. Flight hours 110% pre-COVID per Cirium; CFM56/LEAP overhauls +30% to $1.8 billion at 95% utilization in Singapore. AeroPredict AI +40% to $800 million, 70% base, 35% AOG cuts.

EMEA +28% Ryanair/Lufthansa; APAC +32% IndiGo. $500 million India MRO for 737/A320, Pratt GTF parts. Backlog $25 billion, 85% recurring.

This diversification sets 12-15% FY25 growth, 90% supplier on-time, $2.5 billion capex for 12.5% margins.

Shifting to backlog, a key indicator: total $185 billion record, with funded at $52.6 billion up 8.4% QoQ and 24.3% YoY. Unfunded from F-35/NGAD. Book-to-bill 1.25x, defense 1.35x.

Missiles 42% $53.9 billion +9.8% QoQ: $2.1 billion FMS JASSM/LRASM Japan/Australia AUKUS; PAC-3 Ukraine. Tucson ramps 95% on-time.

Aeronautics 30% $38.5 billion +8.2%: $1.4 billion F-35 Lot 16; $850 million NATO sustainment Poland/Finland; $600 million CCA.

Rotary 18% $23.1 billion +5.5%: $900 million MH-60R India; $450 million AN/APY-10 P-8A.

Space 10% $13.0 billion +2.4%: Vulcan launches, PLEO SATCOM; additive motors -25% leads.

US DoD/NASA 68% $87.3 billion, FY25 $850 billion. International 32% + from Europe 12%, APAC 22%, ME steady.

Validates high-margin tech focus, $500 million IRAD hypersonics/counter-UAS. Supply chain unlocks 15-20% conversion; FY24 revenue $72-74 billion, EPS $28.50-$29.50. Expect 10-12% more growth, 1.1x+ book-to-bill, 13.2% backlog EBIT.

On free cash flow, Q3 $1.2 billion, YTD $2.8 billion +25%, TTM $5.1 billion or 12% revenues—top of 10-12% target, beating peers.

Operating cash $1.7 billion +18%: F-35 Lot 16 $850 million invoiced; services $450 million +30% C-130J/E-2D.

CapEx $450 million 4.2% revenues down from 5.5%, AI predictive at Fort Worth -22% downtime; 40% hypersonics ARRW, 30% space Colorado, rest commercial.

DSO 52 from 61, inventory 4.2x via Patriot insourcing $300 million free.

Regional: DoD $850 billion, NGAD $22 billion; NATO €15 billion Storm Shadow; AUKUS $200 million; ME THAAD $150 million.

Utilization: 40% debt repay $1.0 billion, leverage 1.8x; 30% dividends $400 million 1.8% yield, buybacks $500 million 1.2% shares; 25% R&D $700 million CCA/NGAD; 5% M&A $250 million directed-energy.

De-risks inflation/labor; 98% performance, JSF incentives $120 million. FY24 FCF $5.5-6.0 billion, Q3 $1.4 billion. Funds space/uncrewed $50 billion market.

Aftermarket/services $3.6 billion +25% YoY, 14% of total, 11 quarters double-digit. Commercial 62% $775 million? Wait, segment total 25%, but detail: commercial aviation +22%, defense/gov +12%.

Flight hours 95-110%; LEAP/A320 +28%, 15,000 engines 25,000 TBO ceramic. TrueChoice AI GE partnership 15% efficiencies, $2.4 billion LTSAs Delta/IndiGo mid-teens PPFH.

Defense PBL Lockheed/Sikorsky 98% availability $45 million bonuses; additive titanium blades -30% costs, 28% EBITDA.

North America 55% +20% KC-46/737; APAC +25% ANA/SIA China boom; EMEA +15% Qatar/UK; India +8% HAL Tejas.

Total care bundles 65% backlog; $250 million smart facilities AR/blockchain +22% throughput. Dual-source titanium.

H2 14-16%, $28 billion backlog +19%, $1.8 billion MH-60R; FY $5.0-5.2 billion +200bps to 27%, 7-9% market CAGR.

Finally, priority defense programs amid Indo-Pacific/Ukraine/Israel: Next-Gen Air Dominance F-35 Lot 17/18 $1.8 billion +12%, 156 YTD incl 42 intl UK/Japan/Poland TR-3. Full-rate Lot 17, margins 11.2% +150bps, Block 4 AI EW 95% reliability. NGAD $450 million hypersonic engines GE. Backlog $42 billion +$8 billion NATO.

Hypersonics/missile defense PrSM Lot 2 $950 million +22% $1.2 billion Ukraine/Indo-Pacific; Inc 2 glide 1,200nm CEP<10m Vandenberg. Margins 13.8%, Alabama tunnel. GPI CDR $2.5 billion; Japan $600 million IDIQ, AUKUS $1 billion.

Space Next-Gen OPIR/SDA Tranche 2 $750 million +18%, bookings $1.1 billion; 42-sat IOC 99.9% coverage, optical ML -40% false alarms. Margins 12.5% digital twins. Backlog $28 billion +ESA $4 billion Arctic.

Programs $4.45 billion +16% 72% revenue, margins 12.1% +90bps, book-to-bill 1.3x backlog $125 billion 40% funded. Buffer $2.8 billion cost-plus. Guide Q4 $4.7-4.9 billion, FY 14-16% +$5-7 billion supps, $350 million IRAD HACM/ARC.

David Chen:
Thank you, Elena. Operationally, we've seen significant supply chain improvements, with on-time delivery from key suppliers reaching 92%, up from 72% last year. This has enabled us to ramp production rates on priority programs like the F-35 to 20 aircraft per month and hypersonic missiles to 150 units monthly. We're investing heavily in automation, including AI-driven predictive maintenance across our assembly lines in Fort Worth and Tucson, which has reduced unplanned downtime by 22% and boosted labor productivity 18%. Digital twins and additive manufacturing have shortened lead times for composites and titanium parts by 30-35%, allowing faster backlog conversion while mitigating inflation in rare earths and forgings.

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Thank you, David. On the technology front, we're advancing next-generation propulsion systems, including hypersonic engines tested at Mach 5+ for NGAD demonstrators and boost-glide vehicles with 85% success rates. Our ceramic matrix composites extend TBOs to 25,000 cycles on LEAP equivalents, cutting overhaul needs 20%. In space, optical inter-satellite links and ML threat discrimination deliver 99.9% persistent coverage and 40% false alarm reductions. These innovations, backed by $350 million in IRAD, give us a decisive competitive edge, with early tech transitions to CCA drones and JADC2 integration.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Lisa. Strategically, we are evaluating bolt-on acquisitions to enhance hypersonics and space, like our recent directed-energy laser firm buy to bolster naval DEWs. We're developing outcome-based service models bundling MRO, upgrades, and AI analytics, now 65% of aftermarket backlog. Geopolitics drives this: global spending $2.44 trillion +6.8% SIPRI 2023, structural from great-power rivalry.

Europe NATO 17% surge €380 billion, 23/32 at 2% GDP—Poland 4.1% $2.7 billion F-35/ABMS, Germany €100 billion Zeitenwende Patriot GEM-T 150/year. Our Europe orders +22% hypersonics/counter-UAS Dark Eagle UK/Poland AUKUS offsets 35% local $15 billion sustainment.

Indo-Pacific Taiwan/South China: INDOPACOM $22 billion hypersonics/CCA; AUKUS $368 billion Virginia/Loyal Wingman $4.2 billion; Japan ¥8.9 trillion F-35B SM-6. JASSM drawdown +40% Korea/Taiwan; $450 million IR&D NGAD PL-17 counter, 15% intl growth.

Middle East Israel $24 billion 4.5% GDP $3.5 billion aid Tamir/SkyHunter 1,200/month; Saudi $75 billion THAAD 250/year; UAE $23 billion MQ-9B $1.8 billion. Missiles +28% margins 14.2%, JV hypersonic seekers.

U.S. FY25 $895 billion +4.1%, F-35 TR3 92%, B-21 LRIP, Columbia SSBN; Ukraine $61 billion Stinger/GMLRS $2.1 billion share; hypersonics $28 billion ARRW Mach 20. Book-to-bill 1.6x services +12% ALIS-ODIN.

Multi-domain JADC2 F-35/NGAD/CCA; 7% revenues IR&D $300 million digital twins Ghost Bat/quantum comms. 95% allied sourcing. FY25-27 5-7% CAGR $3 trillion; raised FY24 revenue $72-74 billion +9%, EPS $28.50-$29.50 +12%, 105% FCF/net income.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez:
Good morning, team. Thanks for the details. Can you provide more color on the commercial aircraft delivery rates, particularly supply chain risks into 2025?

Michael Reynolds:
Certainly, John. As Elena outlined, we're mitigating engine bottlenecks through dual-sourcing and forward contracts, hitting 92% supplier on-time. Our $10 billion inventory buffer and flexible backlog clauses protect against GTF prolongations, keeping us on track for 650-700 deliveries in 2025 with pricing power intact.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
Hi, thanks. Curious about backlog growth sustainability given DoD budget risks?

Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, our $185 billion backlog with 1.25x book-to-bill is diversified—68% U.S., 32% international—and anchored by multi-year contracts like F-35 Lot 16 and NGAD. FY25 topline pressures are offset by supps and NATO pledges; we see 10-12% further growth with 13.2% margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Bradley with RBC Capital. Please go ahead.

Tom Bradley:
Thanks. Regarding performance of priority defense programs like hypersonics amid escalating geo tensions?

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Tom, programs like PrSM and GPI are accelerating with Lot 2 approvals and successful Mach 5+ tests, margins at 13.8%. Geopolitical pull from Ukraine/Indo-Pacific adds $5-7 billion upside, backed by our wind tunnels and digital twins for rapid scaling.

Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain laser-focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, innovation, and capturing the multi-year defense upcycle.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
